mechanism: The historical generator emits the default FFFF entry in ClassTerminate, after regular class 1 entries. Its pass 2 emits the default text after those regular texts. The target orders that entry and text first.
implication: The currently demonstrated baseline generator and skeleton output require a changed generation strategy or a compatible postprocessing step to reproduce the target resource layout; merely copying the baseline generated class cannot match.
limits: The original DOS 7 generator implementation and the preferred reconstruction strategy are not established.
This does not imply buildmsg.c is itself part of the target executable or that the baseline C source must be edited.
Other class interleaving and all other resource differences remain separate requirements.
